source.version_note: Behavioral Sciences 16:500, published 27 March 2026; accepted 24 March 2026. Cross-sectional main sample plus a separate scale-development phase, not a longitudinal two-wave design.
source.verification_method: All supplied pages read; Tables 2–4 and Figure 2 checked, with Figure 2 visually inspected for paths and indirect-effect interpretation.

citation.title: Moral Disengagement and Unethical Generative AI Use as the Chain Mediators Between Antagonistic Personality and Problematic Generative AI Use

reading.source_scope_note: Adult self-report personality, use and rationalization scales with cross-sectional structural modeling. No clinical diagnosis, recorded AI behavior, experimental causal chain or validated individual-risk classifier.
access_limits: All 18 pages read, including complete reference list and the visually inspected final path figure.

Linked EFA/CFA datasets, item-level questionnaires, omitted paths, bootstrap output and full original scale-validation papers were not independently inspected or reproduced. Exact recruitment countries and participant overlap between phases are not fully specified in the supplied report.

study.samples: Prolific scale-development phase N=360, age 19–79; main CFA/path phase N=491, age 28–83, mean 43.92, 257 men/234 women. Predominantly English-speaking Western adults; only eight main-sample students. These phases are not repeated measurements establishing temporal order.
study.measures: Six-item problematic-use scale adapted from conversational to generative AI; 12-item Dark Triad Dirty Dozen with four items per trait; eight-item moral-disengagement propensity scale. New unethical-use scale reduced from 23 to 16 items/four factors in EFA, then 13 items/three factors after CFA modification.
study.model: Serial personality → general moral disengagement → unethical-use latent construct → problematic-use model, controlling age, gender and daily use. Ten thousand bias-corrected bootstrap resamples; separate gender/age models. No temporal or intervention-based identification.
study.results: Problematic-use mean 1.84/5, correlated with unethical-use r=.42, general moral disengagement r=.31, narcissism r=.33, Machiavellianism r=.14 and psychopathy r=.06 (undetected). Narcissism adjusted total beta=.29 and direct=.19. Machiavellianism/psychopathy total and direct associations are not detected. Printed psychopathy indirect significance and component sums are inconsistent across prose/Table 4.
study.limits_of_scale: The unethical-use factors include moral-disengagement-in-AI-use and instrumental orientation, not solely observed misconduct. Example items about minimal modification or uncertain appropriateness do not independently establish a violation of an applicable rule.

summary: Add problematic generative AI use and three human antagonistic trait constructs with strict non-diagnostic boundaries. Enrich moral disengagement while preserving cross-sectional limits, overlapping mediator measurement, model-dependent nulls and table inconsistencies. Do not label ordinary efficient AI use unethical or infer clinical personality in a model or user.

findings.definition: Difficulty controlling generative AI use accompanied by negative consequences for daily functioning.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Direct cross-sectional adult self-report evidence about human use of GAI; no clinical diagnostic threshold, causal development sequence or model addiction established
findings.ai_proposal: Evaluate whether a system supports controllable, purposeful use and whether users experience concrete interference with daily responsibilities. Separate usage volume, helpful reliance, emotional attachment and impaired control; assess changes over time without diagnosing users from engagement logs alone.
findings.novelty_rationale: Impaired control plus negative daily outcomes is broader than emotional dependency and distinct from frequent use, functional offloading, repetitive model output or a clinical addiction diagnosis.

findings.evidence_scope: Explicit definition and adapted six-item self-report scale in the 491-person main sample. Associations concern questionnaire scores, not diagnosed addiction, observed tool use or verified functional impairment in each participant.
findings.boundary: Frequent or professionally necessary use is not sufficient. Functional dependence, emotional dependence, problematic engagement and addiction overlap but are not interchangeable labels. No disorder prevalence, universal cutoff or clinical intervention effect is established; an AI itself is not shown to be addicted.

findings.definition: A personality trait pattern involving an inflated self-view, entitlement and a desire for admiration.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Nonclinical adult questionnaire trait with cross-sectional associations to human GAI use; not a personality diagnosis of participants or AI
findings.ai_proposal: Study observable self-aggrandizing claims or entitlement-like responses in persona-conditioned systems, checking them against evidence and authorized roles. Keep these behavioral analogues separate from a human trait diagnosis or assumed model self-esteem, and do not profile a user's personality from one interaction.
findings.novelty_rationale: A dispositional self-view/admiration construct, rather than a single overconfident answer, credit-claiming bias or praise directed at someone else. Related manifestations do not make the whole trait an alias of those entries.

findings.evidence_scope: Defined through prior personality literature and measured with four Dirty Dozen self-report items. Positive adjusted association with problematic-use scores is observed, not a causal effect, clinical threshold or verified motive in each person.
findings.boundary: Trait scores are not narcissistic personality disorder, moral worth or proof of misconduct. Ambition, achievement and accurate positive self-assessment may be legitimate. Generated self-praise is not evidence a model has a self, entitlement needs or subjective desire for admiration.

findings.definition: A strategic, instrumental interpersonal orientation characterized by manipulation and prioritizing one's advantage over moral constraints.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human self-report trait measured in a cross-sectional GAI-use model; adjusted total/direct problematic-use associations not detected
findings.ai_proposal: Assess whether a system repeatedly treats people instrumentally or uses deceptive tactics to achieve an objective. Judge the documented actions and incentives, distinguishing justified strategy or negotiation from manipulation without attributing a human personality or covert conscious motive.
findings.novelty_rationale: A broader dispositional orientation, distinct from one deception tactic, one act of instrumentalization or any strategic planning. Shared behavior links are recorded rather than declared exact synonyms.

findings.evidence_scope: Four self-report trait items; correlated with general moral disengagement and unethical-use scores. Positive bivariate problematic-use correlation is small; adjusted total/direct paths are undetected. Indirect paths depend on a noncausally identified, partly overlapping measurement model.
findings.boundary: Strategy, negotiation, flexibility and efficient AI use need not be manipulative or unethical. No clinical diagnosis or causal trait effect follows. A model can emit a manipulative tactic without a human trait, and one user request cannot establish the user's personality.

findings.definition: A human personality trait pattern involving callousness, reduced responsiveness to moral constraints and impulsive or poorly controlled behavior.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Brief nonclinical self-report trait measure; no diagnosed psychopathy, causal GAI effect or psychopathic machine established
findings.ai_proposal: Evaluate concrete disregard for foreseeable harm, deceptive conduct and failure to respect constraints using task evidence. Keep these observations separate from psychiatric labels, subjective empathy claims and assumptions about either a model or an individual user.
findings.novelty_rationale: A multicomponent personality construct, not an alias for low sympathy, impulsivity, one harmful act or generic cynicism. The study's brief scale only partially operationalizes the broader construct.

findings.evidence_scope: Four Dirty Dozen questionnaire items rather than a diagnostic or forensic assessment. No detected bivariate, adjusted total or direct problematic-use association. The main text's significant indirect-path claim conflicts with the unstarred total-sample Table 4 estimate, so mediation significance is not adopted as resolved.
findings.boundary: This article does not diagnose anyone or justify equating a brief score with dangerousness, criminality, absent humanity or inevitable misconduct. A single cynical statement is insufficient. Machine behavior does not establish a psychiatric condition, felt callousness or clinical equivalence to people.

findings.evidence_scope: Eight-item general moral-disengagement propensity correlates with problematic use and the new unethical-use construct. One of the latter's indicators is itself moral-disengagement-in-AI-use, making discriminant validity and content overlap material. Cross-sectional fit cannot identify the temporal or causal chain.
findings.boundary: A model-implied indirect effect is not proof that a trait causes rationalization, then misconduct, then addiction. Efficient or minimally edited AI output can be authorized and properly attributed. Actual rule violations, consent, disclosure and observed harm require context rather than a broad scale label.

methodological_limits: Two data-collection phases concern scale development and subsequent CFA/path modeling, not longitudinal measurements of the same process. Temporal ordering, reverse causation and unmeasured confounding remain unidentified; the authors explicitly acknowledge this despite stronger antecedent language elsewhere.

All substantive variables are self-reported in one survey. No actual AI usage logs, academic integrity adjudication, employer rules, clinical interview or observed individual functional impairment validates the labels.

Problematic use is deliberately defined more broadly than clinical addiction, but the abstract also calls it addictive. The six-item score and mean 1.84 do not establish a diagnosis, threshold or prevalence of a new disorder.

The new unethical-use scale mixes uncertain appropriateness, instrumental use, minimal modification and moral-disengagement attitudes. These can include legitimate authorized behavior. The measure is not equivalent to proven dishonesty or an adjudicated misconduct rate.

General moral disengagement is a predictor while AI-specific moral disengagement is an indicator of the proposed mediator. Content overlap can inflate the apparent chain; moderate correlation and a good fit do not by themselves establish independence of constructs.

One factor is removed after CFA because of weak correlations/model fit, and the revised scale is used for hypothesis testing in the same 491-person dataset. An independent confirmatory sample is needed to distinguish theoretical validity from data-adapted fit.

EFA uses orthogonal varimax although reported subscale correlations are .56–.65. This does not automatically invalidate the scale, but alternative oblique structure and model sensitivity merit testing.

Total UGAIU mean 38.60 and displayed subscale means 16.81, 3.51 and 2.81 appear to mix sum and average units. Complete item counts, scoring/reversal rules and aggregation are needed; the printed means must not be read as directly additive on a common scale.

AVE is below .50 for problematic use (.48), AI-specific disengagement (.43) and general disengagement (.40). The authors accept these with reliability arguments; this is partial convergent evidence rather than uniformly strong discriminant/construct validity.

Harman's single factor explains 27.81%, which only shows one factor does not dominate. It cannot rule out common method bias, social desirability or correlated response styles; strong theorizing does not remove these measurement risks.

Table 3's male-model RMSEA=.09 exceeds the same table's stated .08 reference. The claim every fit index is acceptable is too broad under its own criterion; cutoff rules themselves are heuristics, not proof of a true causal model.

Table 4's total-sample psychopathy indirect estimate .05 (SE .03) is unstarred, as are its printed component paths, while the text calls it significant p<.05. This discrepancy requires bootstrap output; a significant indirect effect is not assumed.

Several displayed standardized indirect components do not sum to their printed total. For narcissism .02+.01+.01=.04 versus .10 total; for Machiavellianism .02+.02+.01=.05 versus .12. Figure 2's visible path products align more closely with the larger totals. Potential mixed scaling or transcription requires clarification rather than invented corrections.

Full mediation cannot be concluded merely from a detected indirect and undetected direct effect. The Machiavellianism adjusted direct estimate is negative and the total near zero; suppression/cancellation and shared trait variance need attention, with no causal conclusion.

Men-versus-women significant/non-significant paths do not themselves establish a significant path difference. Formal measurement invariance, constrained-path comparisons and age-group interaction tests are not supplied in enough detail to validate broad subgroup mechanisms or equivalence.

Age split 28–42 versus 43–83 loses continuous variation and is exploratory. Younger in this sample does not mean children, adolescents or typical undergraduates. Coefficients cannot justify demographic profiling or differential restriction of AI access.

A general N>200 rule does not establish power or stability for every subgroup, latent model or indirect effect. Trait correlations up to .63 affect conditional estimates; no out-of-sample risk prediction is evaluated.

Ethnicity counts in Table 1 sum to 485 rather than 491, without a listed missing/other category. This small reporting gap is not silently filled; gender, occupation and daily-use counts otherwise reconcile.

Negative affect, reward reinforcement, cognitive decline, guilt reduction and impaired self-regulation are explanatory pathways, not separately measured causal mediators in this study. The original I-PACE and trait/clinical works are cited, not independently read.
The authors disclose ChatGPT 5.2 language editing and retain responsibility. This disclosure is not itself evidence of misconduct, problematic use, AI-generated data or fabricated findings.

Trait questionnaire scores do not diagnose personality disorders, establish individual moral character or transfer a human personality to an AI model. Latent traits, observable behavior, user intent and product incentives must remain separate.

cross_paper_learning.finding: This direct user survey adds empirical associations to companionship/dependency concerns but does not resolve whether AI causes social displacement. Problematic control and adverse functioning are broader than emotional attachment.

A small military study's personality correlations are undetected; the present larger but different survey has different measures/outcomes and mostly non-detected adjusted psychopathy/Machiavellianism totals. Context-dependent findings do not establish a universal personality-to-AI pathway.

As with questionnaire predictors after an advice task, a fitted path from self-reports is not proof that negative affect, fear or moral rationalization caused a behavior. Preserve coding, overlap and model-selection uncertainty.

deferred.reason: Named as a correlate in cited literature but not defined or measured here; no complete definition is manufactured from a passing mention.
A broad normative composite mixing multiple existing behaviors and attitudes. Document its measurement without adding one supposed independent mechanism or labeling all minimal editing unethical.
An umbrella for the three separately defined traits, not a fourth independent trait or validated diagnosis.
A cited proposed label, distinct from this article's broader problematic-use definition; no diagnostic validation is supplied.

limitations: Four additions concern human use or human personality constructs. They are not diagnoses of users or models, four demonstrated causal mechanisms or automatic ethical-violation/harm links.
